statements.__comment: An account's cleanup removes only its own stale edges. A legacy EC2Image node from before per-account image ids can still be RESOURCE-linked from other tenants, and its lastupdated is whichever tenant synced last, so a node-level delete here would drop it from their inventory. aws_ec2_image_orphan_cleanup.json removes nodes no edge refers to.
statements.query: MATCH (:EC2Image)<-[r:RESOURCE]-(:AWSAccount{id: $AWS_ID})<-[:OWNER]-(:AWSOrganization{id: $ORGANIZATION_ID})<-[:OWNER]-(:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID}) WHERE r.lastupdated <> $UPDATE_TAG WITH r LIMIT $LIMIT_SIZE DELETE (r) return COUNT(*) as TotalCompleted

MATCH (:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID})-[:OWNER]->(:AWSOrganization{id: $ORGANIZATION_ID})-[:OWNER]->(:AWSAccount{id: $AWS_ID})-[:RESOURCE]->(:EC2Instance)-[r:HAS]->(:EC2Image) WHERE r.lastupdated <> $UPDATE_TAG WITH r LIMIT $LIMIT_SIZE DELETE (r) return COUNT(*) as TotalCompleted
